name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q01 - Glucose polymer stored by animal tissues

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers of glucose is stored by animals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glycogen is a branched storage polysaccharide of glucose found in animal tissues, predominantly in the liver and skeletal muscles, where it serves as a reserve energy source. In contrast, cellulose is a structural carbohydrate that constitutes plant cell walls, while amylose and amylopectin are the unbranched and branched components of starch, respectively, which serve as glucose storage polymers in plants.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymer of glucose stored by animals is glycogen.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q02 - Identification of non semisynthetic polymer

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not a semisynthetic polymer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Semisynthetic polymers are derived from naturally occurring polymers by chemical modification. Cellulose nitrate and cellulose acetate are semisynthetic polymers prepared by the chemical nitration and acetylation of natural cellulose, respectively. Vulcanised rubber is prepared by introducing sulfur cross-links into natural rubber through chemical heating. In contrast, cis-polyisoprene is natural rubber itself, which is isolated directly from latex secreted by rubber trees without chemical modification, making it a natural polymer rather than a semisynthetic one.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymer that is not a semisynthetic polymer is cis-polyisoprene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q03 - Commercial name of polyacrylonitrile polymer

questiontext.text: The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polyacrylonitrile is synthesized by the addition polymerisation of acrylonitrile (\(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CN}\)) in the presence of a peroxide catalyst. Its commercial names are Orlon and Acrilan, and it is widely used as a synthetic substitute for wool in making commercial fibres. Dacron is the polyester polyethylene terephthalate, PVC is polyvinyl chloride, and Bakelite is a cross-linked phenol-formaldehyde resin.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is Orlon (acrilan).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q04 - Biodegradable polymer identification and structure

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymer is biodegradable?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodegradable polymers contain functional linkages that are susceptible to enzymatic cleavage and microbial decomposition in the natural environment. Poly \(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate (PHBV) is an aliphatic polyester obtained by the copolymerisation of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid. The repeating ester bonds along its backbone undergo rapid bacterial degradation in soil and water. In contrast, synthetic diene rubbers such as polychloroprene (neoprene) and butadiene copolymers, as well as synthetic polyamides such as Nylon 6,6, are resistant to environmental degradation and non-biodegradable.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The biodegradable polymer is poly \(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate (PHBV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q05 - Polymer containing ethylene glycol monomer unit

questiontext.text: In which of the following polymers ethylene glycol is one of the monomer units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Glyptal is a polyester synthesized by the condensation polymerisation of ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) and phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid) with the elimination of water molecules. Thus, ethylene glycol serves as one of its constituent monomer units. Polythene is formed exclusively from ethene monomers, Buna-S is formed from 1,3-butadiene and styrene, and PHBV is formed from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymer in which ethylene glycol is one of the monomer units is glyptal.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q06 - Properties of low density polythene polymer

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is not true about low density polythene?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Low-density polythene (LDPE) is produced by the free-radical polymerisation of ethene under high pressure (\(1000\) to \(2000\text{ atm}\)) and temperature (\(350\) to \(570\text{ K}\)). This free-radical addition mechanism produces extensive chain branching. The branched structure prevents the polymer chains from packing closely together, leading to low density, high flexibility, toughness, and poor electrical conductivity. Because close packing is absent, LDPE is flexible and soft rather than hard. High-density polythene (HDPE), by comparison, consists of linear chains packed tightly together, making it hard and rigid.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The statement that low density polythene is hard is not true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q07 - Monomer unit of polyisobutylene polymer structure

questiontext.text: \(\left[ -\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\underset{\substack{|\\\mathrm{CH}_{3}}}{\overset{\substack{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\\|}}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\underset{\substack{|\\\mathrm{CH}_{3}}}{\overset{\substack{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\\|}}{\mathrm{C}}}- \right]_{n}\) is a polymer having monomer units

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The given polymer structure consists of alternating \(-\mathrm{CH_2}-\) and \(-\mathrm{C(CH_3)_2}-\) units, which corresponds to polyisobutylene. Addition polymerisation proceeds by the opening of the carbon-carbon double bond of the monomer. The alkene containing two methyl groups on one of the vinylic carbons is 2-methylpropene (isobutylene, \(\mathrm{CH_2=C(CH_3)_2}\)). Polymerisation of 2-methylpropene links the head and tail of the monomers to generate the repeating structure \(\left[ -\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2- \right]_n\).

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The monomer unit of the polymer is 2-methylpropene (isobutylene, \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q08 - Polymer formed from caprolactam monomer unit

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymer can be formed by using the following monomer unit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The given structural formula shows caprolactam, a seven-membered cyclic lactam. Heating caprolactam with water at elevated temperatures (\(533\text{ to }543\text{ K}\)) brings about ring-opening polymerisation, producing the synthetic polyamide Nylon-6. Nylon 6, 6 is prepared from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, Nylon 2-nylon 6 is a copolymer of glycine and amino caproic acid, and melamine polymer is synthesized from melamine and formaldehyde.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymer formed by using caprolactam as the monomer unit is Nylon-6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q09 - Polymers requiring at least one diene

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers, need at least one diene monomer for their preparation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diene monomers contain two conjugated carbon-carbon double bonds. Buna-S is prepared by the copolymerisation of 1,3-butadiene (a conjugated diene) and styrene. Neoprene is prepared by the addition polymerisation of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene, also a conjugated diene). In contrast, Dacron is prepared from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid, and Novolac is prepared from phenol and formaldehyde, neither of which contains a diene monomer.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymers that need at least one diene monomer for their preparation are Buna-S and neoprene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q10 - Characteristics of thermosetting crosslinked polymers

questiontext.text: Which of the following are characteristics of thermosetting polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thermosetting polymers are heavily branched or cross-linked network polymers formed from bi- or poly-functional monomers. On heating, they undergo extensive chemical cross-linking in moulds and become infusible and insoluble, so they cannot be remoulded or reused. Linear or slightly branched long-chain molecules that soften on heating and harden on cooling, allowing repeated remoulding and reuse, are characteristics of thermoplastic polymers.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The characteristics of thermosetting polymers are heavily branched cross linked polymers and becoming infusible on moulding so they cannot be reused.

answer.text: Become infusible on moulding so cannot be reused.
Soften on heating and harden on cooling, can be reused.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q11 - Identification of thermoplastic linear branched polymers

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers are thermoplastic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thermoplastic polymers are linear or slightly branched long-chain molecules possessing intermediate intermolecular forces between elastomers and fibres. These polymers soften when heated and harden when cooled, a reversible physical transformation. Teflon (polytetrafluoroethene) and polystyrene are thermoplastics. In contrast, natural rubber and neoprene are elastomers that possess covalent cross-links holding polymer chains together.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The thermoplastic polymers are Teflon and polystyrene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q12 - Polymers used in the manufacture fibres

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers are used as fibre?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fibres are thread-forming polymeric solids displaying high tensile strength and high modulus, resulting from close chain packing stabilized by strong intermolecular forces such as hydrogen bonding in polyamides (Nylon) or dipole-dipole interactions in polyesters (Terylene). Polytetrafluoroethylene (Teflon) is a fluoropolymer used for non-stick surfaces, and polychloroprene (neoprene) is an elastomeric synthetic rubber.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymers used as fibres are Nylon and Terylene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q13 - Identification of addition chain growth polymers

questiontext.text: Which of the following are addition polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Addition polymers are formed by the successive addition of monomer molecules possessing double or triple bonds without the elimination of any small molecular byproducts. Orlon (polyacrylonitrile) is formed by the free-radical addition polymerisation of acrylonitrile, and polystyrene is formed by the addition polymerisation of styrene. In contrast, Nylon and melamine-formaldehyde resin are condensation polymers formed by step-growth polymerisation with the elimination of water molecules.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The addition polymers are Orlon and Polystyrene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q14 - Identification of condensation step growth polymers

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers are condensation polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condensation polymers are produced by repeated condensation reactions between bi- or poly-functional monomer molecules, accompanied by the elimination of small molecules like water or alcohol. Bakelite is formed by the condensation of phenol and formaldehyde with the loss of water, and melamine-formaldehyde resin is formed similarly from melamine and formaldehyde. In contrast, Teflon (polytetrafluoroethene) and butyl rubber are addition polymers formed from unsaturated monomers without loss of small molecules.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The condensation polymers are Bakelite and Melamine formaldehyde resin.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q15 - Monomers forming biodegradable copolymer products

questiontext.text: Which of the following monomers form biodegradable polymers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodegradable polymers can be decomposed by microorganisms under normal environmental conditions. The copolymerisation of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid yields the biodegradable aliphatic polyester known as PHBV. The copolymerisation of glycine and amino caproic acid yields Nylon 2-nylon 6, a biodegradable polyamide. In contrast, ethylene glycol with phthalic acid forms glyptal, and caprolactam forms Nylon-6, neither of which is biodegradable.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The monomer combinations that form biodegradable polymers are 3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid and glycine + amino caproic acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q16 - Examples of synthetic elastomer rubber materials

questiontext.text: Which of the following are example of synthetic rubber?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synthetic rubbers are man-made elastomeric polymers that can undergo vulcanisation and stretch under stress, returning to their original dimensions upon removal of the stress. Polychloroprene (neoprene) and Buna-N (copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile) are synthetic rubbers. In contrast, polyacrylonitrile is a synthetic acrylic fibre, and cis-polyisoprene is natural rubber isolated from rubber trees.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The examples of synthetic rubber are Polychloroprene and Buna-N.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q17 - Polymers possessing strong intermolecular forces

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers can have strong intermolecular forces?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fibres possess the strongest intermolecular attractive forces among polymers, allowing chains to pack closely together and imparting high tensile strength and crystalline character. Nylons (polyamides) exhibit strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between amide groups, and polyesters exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions between polar carbonyl groups. In contrast, rubbers have the weakest intermolecular forces (elastomers), and polystyrene has moderate van der Waals forces.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymers that can have strong intermolecular forces are Nylon and Polyesters.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q18 - Polymers containing vinylic monomer structural units

questiontext.text: Which of the following polymers have vinylic monomer units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vinylic monomer units possess polymerisable carbon-carbon double bonds (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)). Acrilan is prepared from acrylonitrile (\(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CN}\)), polystyrene is prepared from styrene (\(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-C_6H_5}\)), and Teflon is prepared from tetrafluoroethene (\(\mathrm{CF_2=CF_2}\)), all of which are ethylenic/vinylic monomers. In contrast, Nylon is a polyamide synthesized from diamines and dicarboxylic acids or cyclic lactams, which do not contain vinylic units.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The polymers that have vinylic monomer units are Acrilan, Polystyrene, and Teflon.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q19 - Physical property changes upon rubber vulcanisation

questiontext.text: Vulcanisation makes rubber

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Raw natural rubber is soft, sticky at high temperatures, brittle at low temperatures, and easily soluble in organic solvents. Heating raw rubber with sulfur at \(373\text{ to }415\text{ K}\) introduces sulfur cross-linking bridges (\(-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}-\)) between adjacent polymer chains at reactive allylic sites. These cross-links constrain the slipping of chains, making the rubber stiffer, mechanically stronger, less soluble, and more elastic across a broad operating temperature range.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Vulcanisation makes rubber more elastic and more stiff.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q38 - Matching polymers with corresponding monomer units

questiontext.text: Match the polymer of Column I with correct monomer of Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
High-density polythene is an addition polymer formed by the coordination polymerisation of ethene in the presence of a Ziegler-Natta catalyst. Neoprene is a synthetic rubber produced by the addition polymerisation of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). Natural rubber is a naturally occurring polymer formed by the addition polymerisation of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). Teflon is prepared by the addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene. Acrilan is a commercial synthetic acrylic fibre synthesized from acrylonitrile.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
High density polythene matches ethene, neoprene matches chloroprene, natural rubber matches isoprene, Teflon matches tetrafluoroethene, and Acrilan matches acrylonitrile.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q39 - Matching common polymer names with chemical nomenclature

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with their chemical names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nylon 6 is synthesized by the ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam and is chemically known as polycaprolactum. PVC is the standard abbreviation for polyvinyl chloride. Acrilan is the commercial name for the acrylic polymer polyacrylonitrile. Natural rubber is chemically cis-1,4-polyisoprene isolated from rubber trees. LDP is the common abbreviation for low density polythene.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Nylon 6 matches polycaprolactum, PVC matches polyvinyl chloride, Acrilan matches polyacrylonitrile, natural rubber matches cis-polyisoprene, and LDP matches low density polythene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q40 - Matching polymer descriptions with commercial trade names

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with their commercial names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The condensation polymerisation of ethylene glycol with phthalic acid produces the polyester known commercially as glyptal. Copolymerisation of 1,3-butadiene with styrene yields the synthetic elastomeric copolymer Buna-S. Initial linear condensation of phenol with formaldehyde yields Novolac. The polyester produced by condensation of ethylene glycol with terephthalic acid is commercially called Dacron or terylene. Copolymerisation of 1,3-butadiene with acrylonitrile yields the synthetic nitrile rubber Buna-N.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Polyester of glycol and phthalic acid matches glyptal, copolymer of 1, 3-butadiene and styrene matches Buna-S, phenol and formaldehyde resin matches Novolac, polyester of glycol and terephthalic acid matches Dacron, and copolymer of 1, 3-butadiene and acrylonitrile matches Buna-N.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q41 - Matching industrial polymers with primary commercial applications

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with their main applications given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bakelite is a thermosetting polymer with excellent electrical insulating properties, making it ideal for fabricating electrical switches. Low density polythene is tough, flexible, and chemically inert, making it suitable for manufacturing squeeze bottles. Melamine-formaldehyde resin forms hard, heat-resistant surfaces utilized in unbreakable crockery. Nylon 6 exhibits high tensile strength and elasticity, making it ideal for tyre cords and ropes. Polytetrafluoroethane (Teflon) is chemically inert and non-adhesive, making it ideal for non-stick cookware coatings. Polystyrene is lightweight and energy-absorbent, making it widely used as shock-absorbing packaging material.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Bakelite matches electrical switches, low density polythene matches squeeze bottles, melamine-formaldehyde resin matches unbreakable crockery, Nylon 6 matches tyre, cords, polytetrafluoroethane matches non-stick cookwares, and polystyrene matches packaging material for shock absorbance.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q42 - Matching synthetic polymers with mechanism of polymerisation

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with the preferred mode of polymerisation followed by their monomers.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nylon-6,6 is synthesized by step-growth condensation polymerisation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid with the elimination of water molecules. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is produced by the addition polymerisation of vinyl chloride initiated by free-radical catalysts like benzoyl peroxide or persulphates. High density polythene (HDP) is manufactured by the coordination addition polymerisation of ethene in a hydrocarbon solvent using a Ziegler-Natta catalyst at moderate temperature and pressure.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Nylon-6,6 matches condensation polymerisation, PVC matches free radical polymerisation, and HDP matches Ziegler-Natta polymerisation or coordination polymerisation.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q43 - Matching natural and synthetic polymers with characteristic linkages

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with the type of linkage present in them given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Terylene (Dacron) is a polyester formed by the condensation of diols and dicarboxylic acids, containing repeating ester linkages. Nylon is a synthetic polyamide containing repeating amide linkages (\(-\mathrm{CONH}-\)). Cellulose is a plant polysaccharide consisting of \(\beta\)-D-glucose units joined by glycosidic linkages. Proteins are natural polymers of amino acids linked together via peptide (amide) bonds. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is a biopolymer consisting of ribonucleotides joined together by \(3',5'\)-phosphodiester linkages.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Terylene matches ester linkage, Nylon matches amide linkage, cellulose matches glycosidic linkage, protein matches amide linkage, and RNA matches phosphodiester linkage.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q44 - Matching commercial product materials with constituent polymers

questiontext.text: Match materials given in Column I with the polymers given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Natural rubber latex consists of the natural polymer cis-polyisoprene suspended in water. Wood laminates and resin glues are prepared using urea-formaldehyde resins. High-strength ropes and textile fibres are fabricated from synthetic polyamides such as Nylon. Crease-resistant polyester fabrics and garments are woven from Dacron (terylene). Neoprene is a synthetic rubber characterized by superior resistance to oils and weathering. Unbreakable crockery items are moulded from cross-linked melamine-formaldehyde resins.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Natural rubber latex matches cis-polyisoprene, wood laminates matches urea-formaldehyde resins, ropes and fibres matches Nylon, polyester fabric matches Dacron, synthetic rubber matches neoprene, and unbreakable crockery matches melamine formaldehyde resins.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q45 - Matching commercial polymers with repeating chemical units

questiontext.text: Match the polymers given in Column I with their repeating units given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acrilan (polyacrylonitrile) is formed from acrylonitrile and has the repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_n\). Polystyrene is formed from styrene and has the repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)-\right)_n\). Neoprene is formed from chloroprene and has the repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\right)_n\). Novolac is a linear condensation polymer of phenol and formaldehyde consisting of benzene rings linked through \(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\) groups. Buna—N is a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile with repeating unit \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_n\).

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Acrilan matches \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_n\), polystyrene matches \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)-\right)_n\), neoprene matches \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{Cl})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\right)_n\), Novolac matches the linear phenol-formaldehyde structure, and Buna—N matches \(\left(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CN})-\right)_n\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q46 - Semisynthetic rayon properties and cellulose modification

questiontext.text:
Assertion: Rayon is a semi synthetic polymer and is taken as a better choice than cotton fabric.

Reason: Mechanical and aesthetic properties of cellulose can be improved by acetylation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rayon is a semisynthetic regenerated cellulose polymer widely preferred over natural cotton because of its superior texture, sheen, drape, and mechanical strength. Chemical modification of cellulose, such as controlled acetylation or xanthation, modifies the hydrogen-bonding network and enhances its lustre, softness, dye affinity, and mechanical properties. Both statements are accurate, and the improvement in properties achieved through chemical modification of cellulose provides the correct rationale for why rayon is considered a better textile choice than unprocessed cotton fabric.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Assertion and reason both are correct statements and reason explains the assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q49 - High tensile strength and crystallinity of polyamides

questiontext.text:
Assertion: Polyamides are best used as fibres because of high tensile strength.

Strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the carbonyl oxygen (\(\mathrm{C=O}\)) and amide hydrogen (\(\mathrm{N-H}\)) of adjacent linear chains facilitates close, regular packing. This close packing increases the crystalline domain within the polymer, imparting high tensile strength and elasticity. name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q51 - Crosslinking and thermosetting properties of network polymers

questiontext.text:
Assertion: Network polymers are thermosetting.

Reason: Network polymers have high molecular mass.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Network or cross-linked polymers are thermosetting because extensive covalent cross-linking forms an infusible, insoluble three-dimensional network during moulding that cannot be remelted upon reheating. While network polymers do indeed possess high molecular masses, high molecular mass is common to all polymers (including linear thermoplastics like ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene) and does not by itself impart thermosetting behaviour. The thermosetting character is a direct result of three-dimensional covalent cross-linking, not simply high molecular mass.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Assertion and reason both are correct statement but reason does not explain assertion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_POLYMERS_MCQ_Q52 - Properties of polytetrafluoroethene in non stick cookwares

questiontext.text:
Assertion: Polytetrafluoroethene is used in making non-stick cookwares.

Reason: Fluorine has highest electronegativity.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polytetrafluoroethene (Teflon) is employed as a non-stick coating for cookware because it exhibits exceptional chemical inertness, high thermal stability, and an extremely low coefficient of friction, which prevents substances from adhering to its surface. Fluorine is indeed the most electronegative element in the periodic table. While both statements are factually true, the high electronegativity of fluorine is not the functional explanation for the non-stick property of Teflon; its non-stick nature arises specifically from the extraordinary strength and low polarisability of carbon-fluorine bonds that resist chemical interaction.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Assertion and reason both are correct statement but reason does not explain assertion.
